title: Internal fault — hardware failure
shortDescription: Wall Connector detected an internal hardware fault.
fullDescription:
One red blink on a Gen 3 Tesla Wall Connector means the unit has a self-diagnosed internal fault and must be power-cycled. If the fault persists, the Wall Connector itself needs replacement or warranty service.

Always check the Tesla One app for the specific diagnostic — the LED is only a summary.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off the breaker for 60 seconds, then back on.

fixSteps.title: Contact Tesla service
fixSteps.instruction: If fault persists, open a warranty case via Tesla app.

whenToCallPro: If power cycle does not clear the fault.
videoSearchQuery: Tesla Wall Connector 1 red blink fix

faq.a: Yes — Wall Connector has a 4-year warranty.

title: Ground fault detected (GFCI)
shortDescription: Ground fault circuit interrupter tripped — leakage to ground detected.
fullDescription:
Two blinks indicate the Wall Connector's built-in GFCI has tripped because current is leaking to ground. Common causes are moisture in the connector, a damaged vehicle charge port, or a shared neutral in the panel wiring.

Never bypass the GFCI — it protects against electrocution.

fixSteps.title: Inspect connector
fixSteps.instruction: Check for water, dirt, or debris in the charge handle.

fixSteps.title: Try another Tesla
fixSteps.instruction: If possible, test with another Tesla to isolate charger vs car.

fixSteps.title: Electrician inspection
fixSteps.instruction: If fault repeats, have a licensed electrician inspect wiring.

whenToCallPro: If fault recurs after drying the connector.
videoSearchQuery: Tesla Wall Connector 2 red blinks fix

faq.a: It's protective — the fault is what is dangerous.

title: Connector latch fault
shortDescription: Charge handle latch or motor issue.
fullDescription: Three blinks indicate the connector latch mechanism is not working correctly. The latch motor inside the handle releases the connector after charging — if it fails, the car may not start charging or may refuse to release.

fixSteps.title: Inspect handle
fixSteps.instruction: Check the latch tab for dirt or debris.

fixSteps.title: Replace handle assembly
fixSteps.instruction: Tesla service replaces the full cable and handle.

whenToCallPro: If debris clearing does not help.
videoSearchQuery: Tesla Wall Connector 3 red blinks fix

faq.q: Can I replace the handle myself?

title: Overtemperature protection
shortDescription: Wall Connector overheated and throttled or shut off.
fullDescription:
Four blinks indicate the Wall Connector exceeded its thermal limit. Common causes: direct sunlight on the unit, installation in a poorly ventilated garage, or poor wiring connections causing resistance heating at the terminals.

Loose terminal screws are dangerous — have them torqued to spec by an electrician.

fixSteps.title: Relocate or shade
fixSteps.instruction: Shield the unit from sun and add ventilation.

fixSteps.title: Electrician torque check
fixSteps.instruction: Have an electrician verify terminal torque (2.3 N·m).

whenToCallPro: Always, if loose terminations are suspected.
videoSearchQuery: Tesla Wall Connector 4 red blinks overtemp

faq.a: Only a licensed electrician should open and torque-check.

title: Low input voltage
shortDescription: Input voltage below acceptable range.
fullDescription:
Five blinks means the Wall Connector measured input voltage below 200V (for 240V units). Often caused by a shared circuit with high loads, long wire runs with excessive drop, or neighborhood brownouts.

Have an electrician measure voltage at the terminals during peak load.

causes.cause: Wire gauge too small for run

fixSteps.title: Reduce other loads
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off heavy appliances on the same circuit.

fixSteps.title: Measure voltage
fixSteps.instruction: Electrician checks voltage at Wall Connector terminals during charge.

videoSearchQuery: Tesla Wall Connector 5 red blinks low voltage

faq.a: Yes — in Tesla app, reduce max amps.

title: High voltage / overcurrent
shortDescription: Input voltage too high or overcurrent detected.
fullDescription:
Six blinks means the unit saw voltage above 250V or current above rated. Usually a utility issue or a wiring problem between panel and charger.

Have an electrician verify the breaker rating matches the Wall Connector configuration (60A breaker for 48A output).

fixSteps.title: Verify breaker
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure breaker matches Wall Connector DIP switch setting.

videoSearchQuery: Tesla Wall Connector 6 red blinks fix

faq.a: Yes — DIP switches inside set max amps.

title: Wall Connector communication error
shortDescription: Communication issue between Wall Connector and vehicle.
fullDescription:
Seven blinks indicate the control pilot signal between charger and car is unstable. Damaged proximity or pilot pins in the handle, or firmware mismatch between car and charger, can cause this.

Update both the car and Wall Connector firmware, then try again.

fixSteps.title: Update firmware
fixSteps.instruction: Use Tesla One app to push latest firmware to Wall Connector.

fixSteps.title: Inspect handle pins
fixSteps.instruction: Look for bent or dirty pins inside the connector.

videoSearchQuery: Tesla Wall Connector 7 red blinks communication

title: Wall Connector cannot connect to Wi-Fi
shortDescription: Failed to join home Wi-Fi.
fullDescription:
The Gen 3 Wall Connector needs 2.4GHz Wi-Fi. Connection issues come from 5GHz-only networks, hidden SSIDs, or captive portals. Use the commissioning hotspot at setup.

The Tesla One app walks through setup — use it rather than guessing.

fixSteps.title: Enable 2.4GHz
fixSteps.instruction: Create a dedicated 2.4GHz SSID for the charger.

fixSteps.title: Recommission
fixSteps.instruction: Press commissioning button in unit, connect phone to charger Wi-Fi, complete setup in app.

faq.q: Does the charger work without Wi-Fi?
faq.a: Yes — Wi-Fi is only for updates and telemetry.

title: Over-the-air firmware update failed
shortDescription: Firmware update did not complete.
fullDescription:
OTA updates fail when Wi-Fi drops mid-download or Tesla's servers are slow. The charger keeps running the old firmware and will retry automatically.

Force a retry from the Tesla One app or power cycle.

fixSteps.title: Retry update
fixSteps.instruction: In Tesla app → Wall Connector → Update.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Flip breaker for 60 seconds and retry.

title: Breaker GFCI tripped
shortDescription: External or built-in GFCI tripped.
fullDescription:
If a GFCI breaker is upstream of the Wall Connector (required in some jurisdictions), it can trip due to normal EVSE leakage. Tesla Wall Connector has its own built-in GFCI — an additional external GFCI often double-trips.

NEC 2020+ allows the built-in GFCI to satisfy code; many electricians install a non-GFCI breaker for EVSE.

fixSteps.title: Consult electrician
fixSteps.instruction: Verify if external GFCI is required by code — if not, replace with standard breaker.

videoSearchQuery: Tesla Wall Connector GFCI trip fix

faq.a: Wall Connector has built-in — most codes don't require external.

title: Overcurrent protection triggered
shortDescription: Unit measured current above rated — shut off protectively.
fullDescription:
The Wall Connector has internal current limiting. If it sees more than configured DIP switch amps, it shuts off. Misconfigured DIP switches or a faulty vehicle charger can cause this.

Verify DIP settings match the installed breaker.

causes.cause: DIP switches set too low for breaker

fixSteps.title: Verify DIP settings
fixSteps.instruction: Electrician checks DIP switches vs installed breaker.

faq.a: Only up to rated — and only an electrician should change DIP switches.

title: Equipment grounding fault
shortDescription: Ground path to earth is missing or high-impedance.
fullDescription:
Wall Connector requires a continuous equipment grounding conductor (EGC) back to the panel. If the ground wire is broken or the panel ground is loose, the unit refuses to charge.

Never operate a Wall Connector without a verified ground.

fixSteps.title: Electrician inspection
fixSteps.instruction: Test ground continuity from charger to panel and to ground rod.

videoSearchQuery: Tesla Wall Connector ground fault fix

faq.q: Can I chain ground with neutral?
faq.a: No — that violates NEC and is dangerous.
